task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about how residents can take part in Spurwick's review of proposed street-tree removals. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 16, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Spurwick parks office published recommendations concerning 14 street trees after its latest scheduled inspections.
Two trees with storm-split trunks were assigned immediate work, while the other 12 recommendations entered the city's public review process.
The 12 review notices were posted Sept. 15, 2026, with comments due Oct. 6, 2026, under the supplied 21-day process.
The review applies to city-managed street trees, not every privately owned tree visible from the road.
Each notice identifies the tree, the recorded reason for recommending removal and the city office that will receive comments.
Reasons in the current notices include conflicting root and pavement conditions, damage recorded by inspectors and unsuitable space for the tree's mature form.
A submitted objection triggers consideration of the information provided but does not automatically cancel the recommendation.
The parks office can request another inspection or revise its proposal when a comment supplies relevant information not addressed in the first report.
City arborist Tera Venn said, "A useful response tells us what we have missed, not simply whether a tree is loved."
Residents may submit photographs, local observations or questions about alternatives through the city form or a paper submission at the parks office.
The city form is available at https://example.org/spurwick/tree-review, and residents do not need to hire a specialist to comment.
A street association has asked the city to explain replacement planting alongside removal decisions rather than after the work is finished.
Association member Orrin Saye said, "We are looking at the shade over a whole street, not only at the space around one trunk."
Replacement planting is considered separately for site suitability, with no promise that a new tree can occupy the identical position.
The current notices do not contain a total forecast of future canopy loss or growth.
Immediate work on the two storm-damaged trees is outside this comment timetable under the city's supplied emergency-work procedure.
The parks office will publish a decision record for the 12 reviewed recommendations after considering the submissions.
That record will state the final action and the main reasons; a comment count is not treated as a binding vote.
The packet does not establish that all 12 trees are unsafe or that every recommendation will remain unchanged.
Several notice tags are attached to trees planted in a municipal street scheme more than 40 years ago.
The office has arranged a drop-in session to explain the notices, but the session is not an on-site tree-safety assessment.
The procedure described is Spurwick's current local policy, not a statement of tree-removal law in other places.

forbidden_additions: Automatic cancellation after an objection or a binding public vote.
All 14 trees subject to the same timetable or all 12 reviewed trees declared unsafe.
Identical replacement locations or universal legal rules.
preserve: The different immediate-work and review tracks.
How evidence, alternatives and replacement questions enter the local process.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
